flags: Cache confirms the tourism byway name but supplies neither a designation instrument nor the creation, campaigning or construction history of the road. The second paragraph is explicitly corridor history, not an invented road origin.

Used the tourism source’s 150-mile loop rather than material’s 159.5 mapped miles. Driving order follows strip towns: Pelican Rapids, Perham, southern loop/Inspiration Peak, Fergus Falls, Phelps Mill, return. Phelps Mill and Inspiration Peak lack strip mile entries, so their positions use supplied coordinates and regional context; no exact stop mileage asserted.

Current Pelican Pete height corrected from fifteen to 15.4 feet. Dropped its unassigned world-largest claim rather than repeat an unnamed superlative. All substantive current claims were found in cache; Battle Lake naming and Glendalough visitors omitted for focus, not for lack of evidence.
Glendalough’s two cache articles disagree on 1991 versus 1992 state-park chronology. No establishment date reused. No byway driving-time estimate or detailed road geometry is supplied.
Inspiration Peak’s lake count remains Sinclair Lewis’s description, not a promised modern view. Preserved all current titles, coordinates and motifs.
